# Incident Report: STRRAT RAT Infection — 172.16.1.66

**Evidence:** `2024-07-30-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (11,562 frames, 585.7s span, 2024-07-30 06:38:48 to 06:48:34). No IDS/Suricata export was present in the evidence folder; findings are derived solely from packet analysis via tshark.

## Victim host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | 172.16.1.66 |
| MAC | 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08 |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-SKBR25F |
| Domain | wiresharkworkshop.online (DC: WIRESHARK-WS-DC, 172.16.1.4) |
| Logged-in user | ccollier |
| OS (self-reported by malware) | Microsoft Windows 11 Pro, 64-bit |
| Installed AV | Windows Defender |

Identified via NBNS name registration (DESKTOP-SKBR25F), ARP (MAC binding), Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString (ccollier / DESKTOP-SKBR25F$), and confirmed directly by the malware's own C2 beacon fields (below).

## Malware family: STRRAT

**Attribution: signature-confirmed.** The infected host establishes a plaintext (unencrypted) TCP session to an external server and repeatedly transmits a pipe-delimited "ping" beacon that contains the literal string `STRRAT` and matches STRRAT's documented C2 field layout exactly:

```
ping|STRRAT|1BE8292C|DESKTOP-SKBR25F|ccollier|Microsoft Windows 11 Pro|64-bit|Windows Defender|<b64 active-window-title>|1.6|US:United States|Not Installed|<uptime/idle>
```

Fields: family tag, campaign/build ID `1BE8292C`, hostname, username, OS, architecture, installed AV, base64-encoded active window title (keylogger/window-tracking feature), malware version `1.6`, victim country, VNC-installed flag, idle time. This is the malware self-identifying in its own protocol, not an inferred behavioral pattern.

- First beacon: frame 9117, t+76.99s (~06:40:06)
- Beacon interval: ~5 seconds, continuous through end of capture (t+585.66s)
- 102 beacon messages observed total, stream never stops within the capture window

## Indicators of Compromise

**Command-and-control**
- `141.98.10.79:12132` — plaintext TCP, TCP stream 83, source port 49754. No TLS/encryption used for the C2 channel.
- No C2 domain observed; the malware connects to this IP directly (no DNS lookup for 141.98.10.79 precedes the connection).
- STRRAT campaign/build ID: `1BE8292C`, reported version `1.6`.

**Exfiltrated data (via beacon field 8, base64)**
- `SG9tZQ==` → `Home`
- `RG9jdW1lbnRz` → `Documents`
- `cG91bmRzLWZvcm11bGEgW0NvbXBhdGliaWxpdHkgTW9kZV0gLSBQb3dlclBvaW50` → `pounds-formula [Compatibility Mode] - PowerPoint`

These are active window titles captured off the victim desktop, confirming STRRAT's window-tracking/keylogger capability was active and the user was working in a document titled "pounds-formula" in PowerPoint at the time.

**Reconnaissance**
- `ip-api.com` (208.95.112.1:80, plaintext HTTP GET `/json/`, frame 9111-9113) — public IP geolocation lookup, a known STRRAT self-recon step, occurring 1 second before the first C2 beacon (t+75.96s vs t+76.99s).

**Probable payload staging/delivery (observed, not decrypted)**
In the ~13 seconds immediately preceding the first C2 beacon, the host made these TLS connections (SNI-confirmed), consistent with STRRAT's known Java-based delivery chain:
- `github.com` — 140.82.113.3:443 (t+64.05s, 9.9 KB)
- `objects.githubusercontent.com` — 185.199.110.133:443 (t+64.83s, 834 KB transferred)
- `repo1.maven.org` — 199.232.196.209:443 (t+68.01s, **8.9 MB transferred**, 6,540 packets — by far the largest external transfer in the capture)
- `javadl-esd-secure.oracle.com` — 23.194.164.136:443 (t+340s, 48.9 KB) — Java runtime check, consistent with STRRAT's JRE dependency.

These sessions are TLS-encrypted and no TLS key log was included in the evidence, so **no file name or SHA256 hash of the payload can be extracted from this capture.** The large repo1.maven.org transfer is the most likely payload/dependency delivery given its size and timing directly ahead of C2 activation, but this cannot be confirmed to the byte level without decryption.

**No malicious plaintext HTTP downloads were observed.** The only two HTTP transactions in the capture are benign: a Windows connectivity check (`www.msftconnecttest.com/connecttest.txt`, 23.215.55.140:80) and the ip-api.com recon lookup above.

## Summary

Host 172.16.1.66 (DESKTOP-SKBR25F, user ccollier) is infected with STRRAT v1.6 (campaign ID 1BE8292C), a Java-based remote access trojan with keylogging/window-tracking and remote-command capability. It beacons every ~5 seconds to 141.98.10.79:12132 over unencrypted TCP, self-identifying by name in its C2 protocol. Likely delivery involved a large encrypted download from repo1.maven.org shortly before infection activated, but the exact payload artifact could not be recovered from this capture. Recommend isolating the host immediately, blocking 141.98.10.79/12132 at the perimeter, and forcing a credential reset for ccollier given STRRAT's keylogging capability.
